resources.string: Relays carry traffic between devices that cannot connect directly, behind a strict NAT or firewall, and help them find a direct path. Excluding a region matters only for connections that go through a relay: devices that had it as their home relay move to the nearest one left. Latency is the median of what your devices last reported.
Without Tailscale\'s list only the regions the file already excludes are shown.
No relay is left: devices that cannot connect directly will not reach each other.
OmitDefaultRegions is on: none of Tailscale\'s regions are used, only the file\'s own.
Headscale takes its relay map from its own configuration (the derp section of config.yaml), not from the policy. Here is what the file says; it is edited in JSON.
The relay map is written as \"%1$s\". The server reads it; the editor leaves it to JSON.
The relay map is not written as an object of regions. Edit it in JSON.
Regions, or a region number, is written twice; only the last counts. Edit it in JSON.
Replaced by a region in the file
The last relay left; it cannot be excluded
Not written as a region; see JSON

plurals.name: admin_pv_derp_confirm_homes
plurals.item: It is the home relay of %1$d of your devices: %2$s. It will move to another relay, usually the nearest one left. Direct connections are not affected.
It is the home relay of %1$d of your devices: %2$s. They will move to another relay, usually the nearest one left. Direct connections are not affected.

resources.string: Only the file\'s own regions will be left: %1$d. If they fail, devices that cannot connect directly lose each other.
